target: Japanese
native: English

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say jobsite words clearly and greet your crew and coworkers in Japanese.
lessons.focus: Use polite greetings and です for self-introduction. Read hiragana in おはようございます, katakana in ヘルメット, and the reading of jobsite kanji such as 現場 (げんば).

words.note: Katakana marks this borrowed word; also called 安全帽.
親方 is a trade master or crew boss; 職長 is the designated site foreman.
General wrench; スパナ is an open-end wrench.
On site often ネコ or ネコ車 (ねこぐるま); 一輪車 alone can also mean a unicycle.
かなづち: づ is pronounced zu.
Common word for a portable ladder.

words.es: みなさん、おはようございます！

words.note: Natural for checking how a coworker is doing; お元気ですか fits someone you have not seen in a while.

words.en: How do you say "hard hat" in Japanese?
words.es: 「hard hat」は日本語で何と言いますか？

reading.title: Greeting the crew at the jobsite
target: みなさん、おはようございます！
はじめまして。私はカルロスです。
調子はどうですか？
「hard hat」は日本語で何と言いますか？
一輪車はあそこにあります。
トラックは現場の前にあります。
また明日。
native: Good morning, everyone!
Nice to meet you. My name is Carlos.
How are you doing?
How do you say “hard hat” in Japanese?
The wheelbarrow is over there.
The truck is in front of the jobsite.
See you tomorrow.

lessons.speaking: Greet a crew member, say your name, and ask how to say a tool in Japanese, then repeat the tool name clearly.
lessons.openingLine: おはようございます。はじめまして、田中です。お名前は？
lessons.partnerRole: A crew member who greets you, asks your name, and answers your question about how to say a tool name in Japanese.

checks.explanation: おはようございます is a polite morning greeting; the written よう has a long vowel.

checks.prompt: はじめまして。私は____です。
checks.explanation: 私は ... です introduces your name politely; は is pronounced wa.
また明日 means see you tomorrow; 明日 is read あした here.

lessons.sourceObjective: Say jobsite words clearly and greet your crew and coworkers in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give start times, counts and lengths in feet and inches for boards, bags and concrete.
lessons.focus: Read US site measurements in feet, inches, pounds, and cubic yards. Use 時 for clock time, 時間 for duration, 枚 for flat boards, 袋 for bags, and 個 for blocks. The full 0–1,000 number patterns come in later practice.

words.note: A length unit; ready-mix volume uses 立方ヤード (cubic yards) on this US site.
時間 measures duration; 7時 means seven o’clock.
Read いっぷん, さんぷん, じゅっぷん for 1, 3, 10 minutes.
Common jobsite term; 巻き尺 (まきじゃく) is also used.
One bag is ひとふくろ, not いちふくろ.

words.en: We start at 7 in the morning.
words.note: 7時 is しちじ; 4時 is よじ and 9時 is くじ.
20枚 is read にじゅうまい; 枚 counts flat boards.

words.es: 壁の長さは10フィート6インチです。

words.en: The truck is bringing 9 yards of concrete.
words.es: トラックは生コンを9立方ヤード運んできます。
words.note: Means nine cubic yards of ready-mix on this US site; 生コン is ready-mix.

words.en: Each bag weighs 94 pounds, according to the label.
words.es: ラベルによると、セメントは1袋94ポンドです。
この壁用のブロックは250個です。

reading.title: Start times, counts and lengths
target: おはようございます。今日は何時に始めますか？
午前7時に始めて、午後4時に終わります。
8フィートの板が20枚です。
メジャーで壁の長さを測ってください。
壁の高さは8フィート2インチです。
生コンは9立方ヤード、午後2時に届きます。
セメントは1袋94ポンドです。ラベルを確認してください。
native: Good morning. What time do we start today?
We start at 7 a.m. and finish at 4 p.m.
That is 20 boards, 8 feet long.
Please measure the wall length with the tape measure.
The wall is 8 feet 2 inches high.
Nine cubic yards of ready-mix concrete arrive at 2 p.m.
Each cement bag is 94 pounds. Please check the label.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member what time the crew starts and stops, then read the length of 3 boards in feet and inches.
lessons.openingLine: おはようございます。今日は何時に始めますか？
lessons.partnerRole: A crew member who asks what time the crew starts and stops, then asks for the length of the boards in feet and inches.

checks.prompt: 午前____に始めて、午後4時に終わります。
checks.hint: We start at 7 a.m. and finish at 4 p.m.
checks.explanation: 7時 is 7 o’clock; 7時間 means seven hours.
枚 counts flat boards; 本 is used for long lumber.

checks.prompt: セメントは1袋____です。ラベルを確認してください。
checks.hint: Each cement bag is 94 pounds. Please check the label.
checks.explanation: 94ポンド is the labeled bag weight; check the label before using it.

lessons.sourceObjective: Give start times, counts and lengths in feet and inches for boards, bags and concrete.

lessons.title: Identity and Condition
lessons.objective: Say who people are on site and describe what is broken, loose, level or dry.
lessons.focus: Use です to identify people and ～ている for a resulting condition. あります marks where things are. A wall is checked for 垂直 (plumb); 水平 describes a level floor or top.

words.note: Licensed trade title; crews may say 電工 (でんこう).
From ゆるむ, to work loose; ゆるい is the plain adjective (足場がゆるい).
Level for a floor or top; a wall is 垂直 (plumb).
きれい is a な-adjective; also means pretty.

words.en: I'm the foreman on this job.
words.es: 私はこの現場の職長です。

words.en: He's a carpenter and she's an electrician.
words.es: 田中さんは大工で、鈴木さんは電気工事士です。
words.note: Japanese normally uses names rather than 彼/彼女 for coworkers present.

words.es: ここの足場はゆるんでいます。
コンクリートはまだ固まっていません。

words.en: The tools are in the truck.
words.es: 道具はトラックの中にあります。

words.note: The English source says level; on a wall the check is plumb (垂直). 水平 is for a floor or top.

reading.title: Who is on the crew and what condition the site is in
target: 私はこの現場の職長です。
田中さんは大工で、鈴木さんは電気工事士です。
ここの足場はゆるんでいます。
コンクリートはまだ固まっていません。
道具はトラックの中にあります。
壁は垂直ですか？
この板は乾いていますか？
native: I'm the foreman on this job.
He's a carpenter and she's an electrician.
The scaffold is loose here.
The concrete is still wet.
The tools are in the truck.
Is the wall plumb?
Is this board dry?

lessons.speaking: Describe the site to a crew member: say who each worker is, and say whether the scaffold is loose, the wall is plumb (垂直), and the concrete is still wet, using ～ている for a condition that has changed.
lessons.openingLine: 職長さん、今日は誰が来ていますか？
lessons.partnerRole: A crew member who asks who each worker is, then asks about the condition of the scaffold, the wall and the concrete.

checks.hint: I am the foreman on this job.
checks.explanation: 職長 identifies the designated foreman role; 親方 can mean a trade master or crew boss.
ゆるんでいます describes a connection that has come loose. Keep the crew off the scaffold until the designated competent person inspects it.
A wall is checked for 垂直 (plumb); a floor can be 水平 (level).

lessons.sourceObjective: Say who people are on site and describe what is broken, loose, level or dry.
